idiom_name: Link value struct (href/rel/method) in std::vector; dereference via cpprestsdk web::uri / http_client
implementation_notes: C++ has no standard URI type and no std representation of RFC 8288 link metadata, so the producer hand-writes the classic structure: a small Link value type (std::string href, rel, method) aggregated into a std::vector<Link> under a _links member, where C++17 aggregate initialization keeps the declaration as compact as a dynamic-language dict literal. Only the consumer half leans on a library: cpprestsdk's web::uri parses hrefs into immutable scheme/host/path/query components and resolves relative references (resolve_uri, RFC 3986 section 5), and web::http::client::http_client::request(method, path_query_fragment) dereferences the link exactly as an RFC 8288 consumer resolves a relative-reference target; Ada offers a WHATWG-compliant parser when browser-grade URL semantics are needed. Nothing in the language replaces the classic form, so the struct-and-vector realization stays justified whenever the dependency is unwanted - it is then the whole pattern, not a fallback.
pitfalls: Storing href as std::string_view: a view must not outlive the characters it points to, and the std::string::substr temporary trap silently creates a view of a destroyed temporary - links that outlive the response buffer must own their href as std::string.
string_view::data() is not guaranteed NUL-terminated; passing href.data() straight to C-style APIs (e.g. CURLOPT_URL) reads past the view - copy into std::string first.
Passing Link by value re-copies href/rel/method at every hop; transfer const Link& or std::string_view across carrier boundaries to keep the link transfer allocation-free.
Sharing a parsed response across threads is safe only while its buffers stay immutable; a Link viewing a buffer that is later mutated or reallocated is a data race on concurrent dereference.

Emitting hrefs with internal hostnames and ports leaks service topology, and a rel label authorizes nothing - enforce authorization at resolution time and sign or scope links that cross trust boundaries; do not validate URLs with std::regex (documented as unsafe under backtracking attacks).
